bat54a_common_anode.shows: the SOT-23 package with its pins numbered, and the internal circuit beside it: pin 3 is the common ANODE and pins 1 and 2 are the two CATHODEs

bat54a_forward_voltage.assumes: that the shift is linear between the two curves and that it is the same at 0.28 mA as at 0.1 mA. The datasheet plots neither 0 degC nor a tempco directly.
bat54a_forward_voltage.document: Leshan Radio LBAT54ALT1G / S-LBAT54ALT1G, Rev. C (May 2015), served by LCSC for C12743
bat54a_forward_voltage.shows: FIG.1, forward current against forward voltage at seven temperatures. At the 0.1 mA end of the axis the 25 degC curve reads about 0.195 V and the -25 degC curve about 0.285 V, so the forward drop rises about 1.8 mV for every degree the part cools. It is what the trip bus's low level has to be worked out at when the board is declared down to 0 degC.

bat54a_reverse_current.assumes: that 70 degC sits between the 25 and 75 degC curves at about 3 uA, read by eye off a log axis. The datasheet plots no 70 degC curve.
bat54a_reverse_current.document: Leshan Radio LBAT54ALT1G / S-LBAT54ALT1G, Rev. C (May 2015), served by LCSC for C12743
bat54a_reverse_current.shows: FIG.2, reverse current against reverse voltage at seven temperatures. At the 2 V end of the axis - which is where the trip bus holds these diodes - the curve reads about 0.11 uA at 25 degC, 3.7 uA at 75 degC, 12 uA at 100 degC and 27 uA at 125 degC. It is the figure the 10 k pull-up's noise margin has to be set against, and the electrical table's 2 uA at 25 V and 25 degC says nothing about either the voltage or the temperature these actually see.

ref3030_dropout.assumes: the 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 mA points read off the gridlines by eye
ref3030_dropout.document: TI REF3012, 3020, 3025, 3030, 3033, 3040, SBVS032F (March 2002, revised August 2008), served by LCSC for C38423
ref3030_dropout.shows: Dropout voltage against load current: about 10 mV per milliamp to 20 mA, reaching 300 mV at the part's full 25 mA. The features list's headline 1 mV is the unloaded figure, which the description says in as many words - 'Unloaded, the REF30xx can be operated with supplies within 1mV of output voltage'. This board has 129 mV of headroom on 3V3, so what it may draw from VREF+ is bounded by this curve and not by the part's 25 mA output capability.
